stourbridge.s1_head: Stourbridge professional firms and its glass heritage
s1loc: Stourbridge sits in the Black Country glass quarter, where the Glass Cone at Wordsley still marks 400 years of crystal-making and Audnam and Amblecote keep working studios. Around the High Street and Market Street the professional base runs deep: Folkes Worton has advised owner-managed firms here for more than a century, alongside chartered accountants such as TJ Saxon and SRC Accountancy. More than a hundred commercial and business-law firms serve the wider Stourbridge area, regulated by the Solicitors Regulation Authority.

Stourbridge anchors a network of manufacturers, engineers and family firms on business parks toward Brierley Hill and the wider Dudley borough, with Stourbridge Junction linking the town into Birmingham thirteen miles east. widnes.s1_head: Widnes process industry and its business parks
s1loc: Widnes grew from John Hutchinson's 1847 works at Spike Island into a major centre of the chemical industry, later consolidated under ICI alongside neighbouring Runcorn. Many of the old heavy-chemical plants have closed, but process, manufacturing and logistics firms still operate across Halebank Industrial Estate, Widnes Business Park and the sites strung along the Mersey. Sitting in the Borough of Halton between Liverpool and Manchester, the town is served by the M62 and the Manchester Ship Canal.
